html:
The Guna Revolution, also called the San Blas Rebellion, was an uprising of the Guna people of the Caribbean islands of Panama in February 1925 against Panamanian police and officials.

The government of Panama was trying to force the Guna to give up their dress, customs and nose rings, banning the molas, the bright cloth panels their women wore. Police posts on the islands ruled harshly. Led by Nele Kantule and Simral Colman, Guna fighters attacked the police during Carnival, killing about twenty officers and some Guna who had sided with them.

An American diplomat, Richard Marsh, helped them declare a republic, and an American warship arrived. The two sides then agreed to peace, and Panama promised to respect Guna customs. Their land became a reserve in 1938 and later the self-governing region of Guna Yala, east of the Panama Canal. Every year the Guna celebrate the revolution.
sum: The Guna Revolution, also called the San Blas Rebellion, was an uprising of the Guna people of the Caribbean islands of Panama in February 1925 against Panamanian police and officials.
